subject: Post-demo: deployment preference + migration path check-in
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: deployment preference + migration path check-in

Hi Samir — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size the right deployment recommendation.

Demo highlights (short):
- Verified generation latency and sample throughput for the 2-step triage flow
- Showed fallback routing to smaller model for non-critical queries
- Walked through Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs in the console

Open / clarifying items from our side:
1) Migration origin: you mentioned a legacy on-prem GPU cluster running an internal LLM stack (custom serving). Can you confirm whether the current runtime exposes a stable API endpoint or if its tightly coupled to internal batch jobs?
2) Data residency: are there PHI/PII constraints requiring fully air-gapped on-prem, or would a VPC Private deployment (customer-managed VPC + KMS) be acceptable?
3) Traffic shape: expected average QPS during business hours and peak concurrent requests (rough estimate is fine). This matters for Dedicated capacity sizing vs Hosted bursts.
4) SLAs & procurement: any procurement timelines or security approvals we should pace to?

Suggested next steps:
- Quick technical workshop (60m) with your infra/ops team to validate network egress, KMS, and onboarding runbook
- Provide our migration checklist and Dedicated sizing baseline based on answers above

I attached a short pricing baseline for Dedicated to give a ballpark (see attachment). Karthik, looping you to add Dedicated vs Private notes if helpful.

Thanks — happy to set the workshop for early next week.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Samir Patel <samir@aegishealth.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment preference + migration path check-in

Thanks Naomi — great demo, appreciate the clarity. Quick answers and a couple follow-ups: 

1) Migration origin: our current system is a set of containerized microservices fronted by an internal API gateway. We do have an internal HTTP endpoint but it is brittle and not designed for external routing; most traffic is batch inference from nightly jobs. Were looking to (a) migrate realtime patient triage to a managed inference layer and (b) decommission the legacy cluster over the next 4–6 months.
2) Data residency: we handle limited PHI; anything with patient identifiers must remain in our VPC. We cannot use public hosted endpoints for those flows. Non-PHI telemetry could go to Hosted.
3) Traffic: for the triage flow we expect 12–18 QPS average, burst to ~60 QPS peak during certain hours; concurrent live sessions likely 40–80. Nightly batch jobs are heavy GPU load but can be scheduled for Dedicated maintenance windows.
4) Procurement: we're starting the procurement packet next week; security questionnaire will be required for our InfoSec review. Timeline target: pilot by end of Q3.

We can do a tech workshop — ops+infra can join. Proposed windows: Mon/Tue morning ET next week.

Samir
Director, Data & AI Ops
Aegis Health
[Attachment: initial-security-ask.pdf (referenced)]

Samir — perfect, this helps a lot. Short notes inline: 

- Migration origin: since you have an internal HTTP endpoint we can do a staged approach: (1) Private VPC deployment for PHI flows (customer-managed VPC peering + strict KMS/HSM integration), (2) Hosted API for non-PHI telemetry to move fast and reduce cost, and (3) Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable nightly batch windows if you want committed GPU pools for batch jobs.

- Traffic: Based on 12–18 QPS avg and 60 QPS peak with 40–80 concurrent, our initial Dedicated baseline would be 4x A100 equivalents with autoscale headroom; for Private/VPC realtime we recommend 2x A100 equivalents with prefix caching and connection pooling. We'll put numbers in the sizing doc.

- Security questionnaire: attaching a draft we can fill; if InfoSec needs an on-site or additional SOC2 artifact we can expedite via our security team.

Next steps: 
1) Schedule 60m workshop with your infra team (network/KMS/ops) + our infra architect (Marcus) — proposed: Mon Jun 14 09:00–10:00 ET or Tue Jun 15 10:00–11:00 ET. Which works?
2) I'll have Karthik produce a quick Dedicated vs Private one-pager with cost delta and operational tradeoffs and return that before the call.
3) We'll pre-fill the security questionnaire and send it to you 24 hours before the workshop.

Thanks — Ill hold the Mon slot tentatively.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated vs Private quick notes (pre-workshop)

Hi Samir / Naomi — quick note from a sizing/ops perspective ahead of the workshop.

Tradeoffs at a glance: 
- Private VPC (recommended for PHI): pros = full network isolation, customer KMS, audit logs; cons = longer setup (VPC peering, firewall rules), SLA depends on customer infra for networking.
- Dedicated capacity (recommended for batch and predictable throughput): pros = reserved GPU pool, lower unit cost at scale, simpler maintenance; cons = higher committed spend, still requires secure ingress for PHI flows unless combined with Private.
- Hybrid approach: keep PHI on Private, tier non-PHI onto Hosted with a routing policy. This gives fastest time-to-value while keeping compliance-bound traffic isolated.

Operational asks for the workshop: VPC CIDR ranges, egress IP allowlist for onboarding, KMS key ARN example, and a sample peak QPS trace (raw CSV OK). If you can drop those in the HubSpot record HS-4821 or share a Drive link ahead of time well pre-populate the runbook.

Ill bring a short deck (2 slides) with estimated cost delta for the pilot (pilot = 6 weeks, non-production).

-Karthik
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
